title: Wayfare Pass Frequent-Rider Restoration Discount — Questions and Answers
content:
# Frequent-rider restoration discount — Wayfare Pass (rider membership)

**What is the frequent-rider restoration discount?**
On the restoration of a past-due Wayfare Pass membership, the frequent-rider restoration discount counts the member's trips charged a fare in the last three months: 5 percent at 12 or more such trips, 2 percent at 6 to 11, nothing below 6.

**Which records are counted?**
The fare charges on the member's trips in Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares): each fare charge dated in the last three months counts as one trip charged a fare. Other trip charges, such as waivers, tips or fees, are not fare charges.

**How does the discount act on the payment?**
It is taken off the restoration payment as that percentage of the membership fee the payment collects for the period in force. The percentage is of that membership fee amount itself; the amount taken off is not rounded on its own, and the payment is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Where are the tier edges?**

| Trips charged a fare in the last three months | Discount |
|---|---|
| 12 or more | 5 percent |
| 6 to 11 | 2 percent |
| 0 to 5 | nothing |

12 trips earn 5 percent while 11 earn 2 percent; 6 trips earn 2 percent while 5 earn nothing.

**Can you show a figure?** (hypothetical)
A member restoring a Wayfare Pass Plus Monthly membership whose payment collects the full 19.99 fee, with 7 fare charges in the last three months: 2 percent of 19.99 is 0.3998, leaving 19.5902, which rounds to 19.59.
